reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage as a way to earn BNB through slot activation, claiming “50% of activation” and “5 5 times more.” It directs viewers to join through a specific link and contact the speaker, while promising money will reach a linked wallet rapidly. These activation-based return claims are tied to a direct financial-participation solicitation.

✓ Join Forsage with this link; https://forsage.io/b/txmg1d.
Forsage xQore Program - Earn BNB with Forsage Platform
if you are interested in Forsage contact us I will guide you properly.

opening.argument: The available wording does not establish a guaranteed result or concealment of risk. The speaker describes a program feature in qualified, imperfectly clear terms, saying it is a “latest new metric” and that returns depend on both the viewer getting a slot and the team getting one. The claim therefore leaves important conditions unresolved rather than proving a fixed outcome for every participant. The speaker also characterizes the system as decentralized and says transactions go directly to a linked wallet, which presents a technical description, not proof that viewers will profit. On this record, the evidence supports a discussion of an alleged blockchain program whose operation and results require independent verification, not a conclusively deceptive promise.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats “50%” and “5 5 times more” as a guaranteed return, but the quotation does not say that every viewer will receive either amount, nor does it explain whether these are conditional program mechanics, examples, or a mistranscribed statement. The link and invitation to contact the speaker establish an entry point for information, but do not by themselves establish deception or a guaranteed financial outcome. The record also does not show that money was taken, that anyone lost money, or that the speaker concealed a material condition.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The conditional wording does not make the promotion a warning; it describes the conditions for receiving the stated payout. The speaker expressly connects the viewer’s slot and the team’s slot to “50% of activation” and says activation produces “5 5 times more.” The title also presents the program as a way to “Earn BNB,” while the description supplies a joining link. Whatever ambiguity remains about the mechanics, the overall message is a financial recruitment pitch, not a neutral risk disclosure.

opening.argument: The speaker explicitly frames the content as explaining a program: “In this video I'm gonna discuss about Forsage X-Core Program.” The subject is presented as decentralized blockchain technology and a transaction process involving a linked wallet. That is consistent with an operational or technology-oriented explanation of how a platform is described to work. The available frames show the speaker addressing the camera, but they do not show a payment screen, enrollment record, or demonstrated outcome. A contact invitation may offer further guidance, yet the supplied evidence does not establish that the video itself executes a transaction or proves a profit claim. The strongest grounded reading is an explanation of a blockchain program and its asserted features, whose claims remain to be checked.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a discussion does not erase its subject matter, but the prosecution still has to show what the video actually establishes. The supplied text does not document a completed enrollment, a payment, or a verified payout. Nor do the frames supply operational evidence beyond a person speaking to camera. Thus, the material can reasonably be treated as a verbal explanation of a platform’s claimed operation rather than proof that the platform is fraudulent.

This is not merely a technical walkthrough: the speaker states that activation yields multiplied returns, identifies themself as a team leader, asks interested viewers to make contact, and the description directs viewers to join. No payment screenshot is needed to establish that the video promotes participation in a return-generating slot system.

opening.argument: The evidence can also be read as ordinary referral promotion for access to an external blockchain service, not proof of a scam mechanism. The description provides a referral-style link, and the speaker offers to guide interested people; those facts establish promotion, but not that the service is unsafe. Crucially, the record does not show a request for passwords, credentials, identity documents, or private keys. It does not show an actual deposit, a completed transaction, a guaranteed return, or a downline payment. The speaker’s description instead says funds would move to a linked wallet directly and quickly, while the system is described as decentralized. The payout language warrants scrutiny, but the supplied material alone does not establish the full mechanism needed to classify ordinary referral promotion as fraudulent.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of credentials or a visible deposit does not answer the central claim. The prosecution relies on the speaker’s own description of activation-linked returns, not on an invented password request or a visible transaction. A referral link and personal guidance are ordinary promotional features that can accompany legitimate services. The supplied record does not establish who controls the link, whether participation requires payment, or how the percentages operate, so the alleged mechanism remains underdetermined.

The title and link make the promotion concrete, and the speaker offers personal guidance to interested participants. Those facts show solicitation into a tiered participation structure even if the video does not display a payment screen or explain every technical detail.
